newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian stocks to take lead from U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Belgian stocks to take lead from U.S. market.

text.p: Wall Street's overnight performance will provide the lead for Belgian shares at the start of next week, after markets were depressed on Friday by U.S. rate rise worries due to stronger-than-expected data.

The Bel-20 index .BFX closed 6.17 points or 0.29 percent lower at 2,114.52, sliding into the red after U.S. retail sales and producer price data. The Dow Jones .DJI stood 72 points or 1.1 percent lower at 6,467 after falling to 6,448.
"The figures were worse than expected, but I am surprised by the fall," one dealer said. March PPI fell 0.1 pct, but excluding food and energy rose a higher-than-forecast 0.4 pct.
Retail sales rose a less-than-forecast 0.2 percent, but February's figure was revised upwards.
Analysts said that fundamentally the picture in Europe was quite positive for stocks, but there was a risk U.S. investors would sell European shares as they lowered their exposure to U.S. equities.

Friday saw below-average volume in Brussels amounting to two billion francs worth of Belgian shares, and causing exaggerated spreads in some stocks like BBL, which ended up 20 francs at 7,800. Of the Bel-20 index component stocks, five ended higher, five unchanged and 10 lower.
Chemicals and drugs firm UCB was among gainers, rising 0.22 percent to 89,400 francs, though the bid-ask spread was 150 francs and only 1,002 shares were traded.
After the market closed UCB said final current profit had risen 33 percent in 1996 and that it would propose a net dividend of 750 francs per share against 600 last year.
